visual_bible.style: Original 2D Historical Chibi Animation (Q-Version Cartoon) world. Clean rounded dark outlines, simplified legible shapes, flat colors and restrained two-tone cel shading. Apply Q-Version anatomy only to people actually present. Maps and cutaways use the same hand-drawn contour language.
visual_bible.palette: Warm ochre/sand terrain, pale cream, teal-blue water, muted olive vegetation, dark charcoal outlines. Color supports real subject identity; hypothetical state is labeled rather than inferred from color alone.
visual_bible.world: Sahara-related illustrative scenes and fictional contemporary intervention. Landscapes are reconstructions, not exact surveyed views. Diagrams are explanatory simplifications, not measurements or forecasts.
visual_bible.linework: Consistent confident rounded dark outlines; no photorealism, 3D or paper collage.
visual_bible.environment_design: Geography, water, installed pipes and ecological links can lead without people. Adjust detail density to the view and knowledge task.
visual_bible.scale_rules: Do not extrapolate the illustrative water box into a measured Sahara forecast. Earth/map shapes and ocean direction remain geographically legible. Aquifer section is schematic, not a measured geological profile.
continuity_rules: Water stays teal-blue and terrain ochre throughout
Follow source -> resource accounting -> decision -> conditional aftermath -> connected ecosystems
No named protagonist cameos in character-free scenes
Preserve branch and explicit illustrative status across scene changes

characters.status: fictional one-off operator for this sample
characters.description: Adult survey engineer, rounded oversized head and compact Q-Version body, short black hair, cream wide-brim sun hat, teal work shirt, tan trousers, charcoal boots. Calm focused expression. Present-day clothing is a design choice, not a historical witness.
characters.continuity: Identity only; pose, distance and frame occupancy follow the decision scene. Do not insert Minh in other shots.

beats.narration_span: Paragraph 1 opening: freshwater lakes in Ounianga, an engaging subject before assignment

shots.scene: A very wide high-oblique illustrative Sahara vista inspired by Ounianga: several long dunes separate deep teal freshwater lake surfaces, sparse reed fringes near water, ochre rocky desert continuing to the far horizon. The water and surrounding dry landscape are the main subject, not a settlement or a character. Do not claim an exact recreation or add lush vegetation across the desert.

visual_intent.primary_subject: lake water within a much larger dry landscape
visual_intent.hierarchy: lake shapes and dry extent readable first; sparse details
visual_intent.transition: the teal lake surface leads into the water-source cutaway

scenario_context.basis: Scoped NASA Ounianga explanation; not a surveyed photograph

animation.keyframe: Lake water lies between dry dune ridges with a broad dry horizon
animation.action: Let the viewer read the geographical contrast
animation.end: The lake water is the visual question for the next scene
animation.camera: subtle horizontal pan, preserve lake edges
animation.framing: extreme-wide high oblique view, uneven natural dune/lake shapes
animation.continuity: Same ochre terrain and teal water in the section that follows

beats.narration_span: Paragraph 1 ending and paragraphs 2–3: the hidden source, changed historical conditions and the question of what sustains vegetation

shots.scene: A clean schematic ground cutaway beneath a small desert lake. A connected blue groundwater-bearing layer below ground reaches the lake basin; a few clear blue upward flow arrows show groundwater reaching the surface. Dry ochre soil above, simplified rock layers below, a small reed fringe only by the lake. Do not draw a limitless subterranean ocean, an invented recharge rate or a hydraulic pipe as the natural source. No exact geological measurement implied.
shots.text_placement: one large dark label above the cutaway on its cream diagram area; use the arrow glyph exactly; no other letters or numbers

visual_intent.hierarchy: connected blue water layer and flow arrows dominate; simplified few layers
visual_intent.transition: blue source becomes the water resource that the operator must audit

scenario_context.basis: C1-C2; schematic mechanism, no measured aquifer profile
scenario_context.uncertainty: No renewable supply rate is established

animation.start: One visible connected water-bearing layer and lake
animation.keyframe: The cutaway makes the hidden supply-to-lake relationship readable
animation.action: Hold on the relationship; arrows are explanatory drawing elements
animation.end: Viewer recognizes the source as a resource requiring accounting
animation.framing: close section view with open cream space and a small surface above
animation.continuity: Teal lake from S01; simplified terrain layers with shared linework

beats.narration_span: Paragraphs 4–6: the fictional project delays expansion to audit water before buying plants

shots.scene: At an open desert field-work table, fictional operator Minh deliberately places a large water-allocation map above a small tray of seedlings, making the supply audit the priority. One gloved hand indicates the blue supply line on the map; the other holds a pencil still. No presenter pose or giant portrait. Map and deliberate choice are the focus; sparse desert behind. No additional people and no readable map letters.

visual_intent.primary_subject: water-map audit taking priority over seedling purchase
visual_intent.representation: human action in a medium three-quarter scene
visual_intent.hierarchy: hands, blue map route and seedlings readable; character expressive but not frame-filling
visual_intent.transition: the map's bounded plot leads into the area/depth budget diagram

animation.start: Minh is already consulting the map
animation.keyframe: The audit decision is visible in hand placement and map above seedlings
animation.action: Hold the decision at its clearest instant; do not depict multiple hand positions
animation.end: The visible blue supply line motivates the budget explanation
animation.camera: gentle short push-in on hands and map
animation.framing: medium three-quarter view, entire head/body readable without crowding the map
animation.continuity: Minh identity from the visible spec; teal water line remains the motif

beats.narration_span: Paragraphs 7–12: illustrative area × additional net depth consumes the cap before extra costs; not a measured requirement

shots.scene: An uncluttered 2D explanatory diagram on cream: a flat ochre land rectangle with a thin translucent teal water layer demonstrates area times water depth. Beside it, a simple bounded blue water-volume container stands at its illustrated cap with zero reserved headroom. This is a conceptual unit diagram, not a real terrain model, a software interface or a forecast. Preserve 2D flat/cartoon linework, no photorealistic water and no character or anthropomorphic equipment.

shots.text_placement: three clear large dark diagram labels, arranged on cream above and below the conceptual area/water relationship, keep the equation on one readable line; no extra text

visual_intent.function: explain quantitative scale and a constraint
visual_intent.primary_subject: area, net depth and limited volume
visual_intent.representation: diagram with a deliberately designed comparison of need and cap
visual_intent.hierarchy: equation and blue quantity dominate; sparse shapes with generous negative space
visual_intent.transition: budget limit prepares the conditional result and site obligations

scenario_context.basis: Only A2-A4 illustrative inputs; correct units, not measured irrigation demand
scenario_context.uncertainty: The original source does not establish actual site/species demand or viable project design

animation.keyframe: Net need equals the assumed cap before additional needs
animation.action: Hold for labels and quantity relationship; do not create a character reaction
animation.end: Viewer understands the lack of headroom
animation.framing: flat diagram composition with large labels, no dense scenic backdrop
animation.continuity: Same blue supply motif and ochre land; exact assumed quantities from narration

beats.narration_span: Paragraphs 13–14: after deployment and cancellation, installed infrastructure and obligations persist

shots.scene: A quiet ground-level long view of a fictional stopped pilot site: a closed blue-grey irrigation valve and installed pipe in the near foreground, sparse unused planting rows and a small locked equipment shelter beyond. The pipe remains intact; some modest vegetation survives near an outlet, the wider desert remains dry. Show a lingering constructed state, not an apocalyptic wasteland or proven ecological devastation. No person or mourning face. The old water line now ends at a closed valve.
shots.text_placement: one short large phrase on a plain illustrative field placard beside the valve, legible within wide framing; no official logos or invented project title

visual_intent.function: show consequences that remain after failure
visual_intent.primary_subject: installed infrastructure and changed site after stopping
visual_intent.hierarchy: near valve versus lingering site depth; restrained details
visual_intent.transition: the local pipe/source motif opens into a wider question about connected systems

scenario_context.basis: A5/R1; invented site, not a documentary record
scenario_context.uncertainty: No quantified damage or exact future loss is claimed

animation.start: The pilot site is already stopped
animation.keyframe: Closed valve and installed pipe visibly persist
animation.action: Hold the consequence rather than stage a character reaction
animation.end: World retains infrastructure and maintenance responsibility
animation.camera: slow restrained horizontal pan along the pipe, then hold
animation.framing: low wide view with a dominant near object and quiet site depth
animation.continuity: Teal/blue supply motif now closed; warm ochre/cream style preserved

beats.narration_span: Paragraphs 15–19: explicitly reorient into added conditional success assumptions, then consider the actual dust/nutrient link without certain future ecosystem/climate claims

shots.scene: A simplified hand-drawn 2D Atlantic-basin map: northern Africa/Sahara on the right/east, northeast South America/Amazon on the left/west, teal Atlantic between them. A restrained ochre dust ribbon/arrows travels westward from the Sahara toward the Amazon, with a modest patch of olive rainforest canopy at the receiving end. Keep actual continent silhouettes geographically legible, not mirrored. This shows the established nutrient transport connection, not a predicted future change, dying Amazon, inevitable greening feedback or anthropomorphic planet. No people.

visual_intent.hierarchy: two continents, connecting route and receiving vegetation; readable sparse layout
visual_intent.transition: Narration explicitly introduces B1 conditions before widening to the established connection; do not imply failure causes this transport or draw a certain future outcome

scenario_context.basis: C4 actual dust connection; R3 future modification remains conditional
scenario_context.uncertainty: No amount of change or certain forest/climate outcome is depicted
